title: The concrete square-zero obstruction and its power-lifting criterion
statement: Let j:Z\to X be a closed immersion [def-weil-closed-immersion] of schemes [def-pc-scheme], L an invertible module [def-sc-invertible-module], and I=j.\ker [def-sbc-closed-immersion-ideal-sheaf] with I^2=0 [def-sbc-ideal-sheaf-powers]. For n\ge0 and s a global section of N=(j^*L)^{\otimes n}, with tensor pullback [def-pc-module-pullback], put F=j^*(I\otimes L^{\otimes n}). Then F is quasi-coherent [def-pc-quasi-coherent-sheaf]. There exists xi in H^1(Z,F) [def-sc-ringed-space-module-cohomology] such that for every e\ge0, if the map on H^1 induced by F\simeq F\otimes O_Z\to F\otimes N^{\otimes e}, v\mapsto v\otimes s^{\otimes e}, kills xi, then there are a global section t of L^{\otimes n(e+1)} and an isomorphism a:j^*(L^{\otimes n(e+1)})\simeq N^{\otimes(e+1)} which sends the restriction of t under the canonical adjunction unit [lem-pc-module-pullback-adjunction] to the (e+1)st tensor power of the section morphism of s. No compactness, Noetherianity, or affine nonvanishing-open assumption is imposed.

source.place: Cohomology of Schemes, Lemma 09MS, equation (30.17.5.1) and the square-zero section-power lifting argument; https://stacks.math.columbia.edu/tag/09MS

proof.text: Put N=j^*L. The closed-immersion ideal sequence tensored by the invertible L^d is exact, with kernel M_d=I tensor L^d and quotient j_*j^*(L^d), by the unit-quotient theorem. Pullback commutes with tensors, so identify the quotient with j_*(N^d). The ideal I and M_d are quasi-coherent, and I M_d=0 because I^2=0. The annihilated-module theorem identifies M_d with j_*G_d, where G_d=j^*M_d is quasi-coherent. The affine-morphism cohomology edge identifies H^1(X,M_d) with H^1(Z,G_d). The given section s of N^n has a connecting class xi in degree n.

source.place: Cohomology of Schemes, Lemma 09MS, equation (30.17.5.1) and the square-zero section-power lifting argument; https://stacks.math.columbia.edu/tag/09MS

proof.text: Set O'=direct sum over m>=0 of L^{tensor m} and O=direct sum over m>=0 of j_*j^*L^{tensor m}, with multiplication by tensor product. These are sheaves of commutative O_X-algebras: locally a frame for the invertible L identifies O' with a polynomial algebra in one generator, so its multiplication is commutative; the quotient O is commutative too. The degreewise surjection from step 1 gives O' \to O with kernel K=direct sum over m>=0 of I tensor L^{tensor m}; products of two kernel terms land in I^2 tensor L^{tensor (a+b)}=0. Apply [lem-sc-boundary-derivation-square-zero] to O' \to O. By naturality of the long exact sequence for inclusion of a degree-m summand and projection onto it, projecting the boundary of the summed sequence to degree m is the boundary of the degree-m exact sequence. Thus the image of s in the degree-n summand has boundary xi. Induct on k>=1: for k=1 this is xi; if partial(s^k)=k s^{k-1}xi, the Leibniz rule gives partial(s^{k+1})=s partial(s^k)+s^k partial(s)=(k+1)s^k xi. Taking k=e+1 gives partial(s^{e+1})=(e+1)s^e xi, where s^e acts through O on K.

For any exponent e annihilating the transported boundary class, naturality identifies the displayed H^1 map with multiplication by s^e. The derivation formula makes the degree n*(e+1) boundary vanish. Exactness then supplies a lift; the tensor-pullback comparisons identify its restriction with the (e+1)st power.

theorem exists_square_zero_section_power_obstruction
    {X Z : Scheme.{u}} (j : Z ⟶ X)
    [IsClosedImmersion j]
    (L : X.Modules) [L.IsInvertible] (hI : j.ker ^ 2 = ⊥)
    (n : ℕ) (s : (((tensorPullback j).obj L).tensorPow n).val.presheaf.obj
      (Opposite.op ⊤)) :
    let F := (tensorPullback j).obj (j.ker.toModules ⊗ L.tensorPow n)
    F.IsQuasicoherent ∧ ∃ (xi : (RingedSpace.moduleCohomology Z.toRingedSpace 1).obj F),
      ∀ e : ℕ, (RingedSpace.moduleCohomology Z.toRingedSpace 1).map
        ((ρ_ F).inv ≫ F ◁ tensorPowSection (homOfGlobalSection
          (((tensorPullback j).obj L).tensorPow n) s) e) xi = 0 →
      ∃ t : (L.tensorPow (n * (e + 1))).val.presheaf.obj (Opposite.op ⊤),
        ∃ a : (tensorPullback j).obj (L.tensorPow (n * (e + 1))) ≅
            (((tensorPullback j).obj L).tensorPow n).tensorPow (e + 1),
          homOfGlobalSection ((tensorPullback j).obj (L.tensorPow (n * (e + 1))))
              (((Classical.choose (exists_tensorPullbackAdjunction j)).unit.app
                (L.tensorPow (n * (e + 1)))).val.app (Opposite.op ⊤) t) ≫ a.hom =
            tensorPowSection (homOfGlobalSection
              (((tensorPullback j).obj L).tensorPow n) s) (e + 1)
